verses.text: “Be careful not to do your good deeds in front of people just so they’ll see you. If you do, your Father in heaven won’t reward you.

“So when you give to people in need, don’t announce it with a trumpet like the hypocrites do in synagogues and on the streets so people will praise them. I’m telling you the truth: they’ve already received their reward.
But when you give to people in need, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so your giving stays private. Your Father, who sees what’s done in private, will reward you.

“When you pray, don’t act like the hypocrites. They love to stand and pray in synagogues and on street corners so people will notice them. I’m telling you the truth: they’ve already received their reward.
But when you pray, go into a private room, shut the door, and pray to your Father who is unseen. Your Father, who sees what’s done in private, will reward you.
“When you pray, don’t keep repeating empty phrases like the Gentiles do. They think their many words will make them heard.
Don’t be like them. Your Father already knows what you need before you ask him.
“Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be honored as holy.
May your Kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us the food we need today.
Forgive us our debts, just as we forgive those who owe us.
Don’t bring us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. The Kingdom, power, and glory are yours forever. Amen.’
“If you forgive others when they wrong you, your Father in heaven will forgive you too.
But if you don’t forgive others when they wrong you, your Father won’t forgive your wrongs either.

“When you fast, don’t put on a gloomy face like the hypocrites. They make themselves look miserable so people will see they’re fasting. I’m telling you the truth: they’ve already received their reward.
But when you fast, put oil on your head and wash your face,
so people won’t see that you’re fasting, but your Father who is unseen will. Your Father, who sees what’s done in private, will reward you.
“Don’t store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moths and rust destroy them, and thieves break in and steal.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where moths and rust can’t destroy them and thieves can’t break in and steal.
Because wherever your treasure is, that’s where your heart will be too.
“The eye is the body’s lamp. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is unhealthy, your whole body will be full of darkness. If the light inside you is actually darkness, that darkness is intense.
“No one can serve two masters. You’ll hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and look down on the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
“So I tell you, don’t worry about your life—what you’ll eat or drink, or about your body and what you’ll wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothes?
Look at the birds in the sky: they don’t plant, harvest, or store food in barns, but your Father in heaven feeds them. Aren’t you worth much more than they are?
Can any of you add even a moment to your life by worrying?
And why worry about clothes? Look at the wild lilies and how they grow. They don’t work or make clothing for themselves,
but I tell you, even Solomon in all his glory wasn’t dressed as beautifully as one of them.
If God clothes the field’s grass like that—even though it’s here today and tomorrow gets thrown into the oven—won’t he take even more care of you, you who have so little faith?
“So don’t worry and say, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
The Gentiles chase after all these things, but your Father in heaven already knows you need them.
Make God’s Kingdom and his righteousness your first priority, and all these things will be provided for you too.
So don’t worry about tomorrow. Tomorrow will have its own worries. Today already has enough trouble of its own.
